paper.title_en: Constriction-Type Superconducting Quantum Device Modified by Local Thermal Effect
paper.abstract_en: We report a method to locally modify superconducting materials using nano-laser direct writing, rather than conventional ablation or etching, for the fabrication of constriction-type Josephson junctions and superconducting quantum devices. Specifically, at a fixed laser power of 120 mW, the critical current $I_c$ can be modified from 250 $\mu $A to 80 $\mu $A by increasing the pulse width from 3.0 ms to 4.0 ms, establishing an optimal processing window prior to the onset of irreversible film degradation. The optimized SQUID operated at 4.0 K exhibited a voltage-flux modulation depth of approximately 200 $\mu $V, a maximum flux-to-voltage transfer coefficient $V_{\varPhi }$ of 0.75 mV/$\varPhi _0$, and a white flux noise spectral density of 2 $\mu \varPhi _0$ Hz$^{-1/2}$. With its ability to locally modify superconducting properties without material removal, this approach opens new avenues for in-situ tunable Josephson junctions and provides a flexible platform for future superconducting quantum circuits.
